summary: Steel observation tower on Massanutten Mountain, built 1935 by the CCC; a standing day-use Forest Service observation site reached by a four-mile road.

access.note: Day-use site open year round, sunrise to sunset, no fee; access subject to Virginia DOT closures; no potable water on site

visit.trail_note: Drive Woodstock Tower Road (SR 758) about four miles to the top of the mountain; the footpath to the tower is on the left

events.note: Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps; materials or funds from the Woodstock Chamber of Commerce (sources differ)
Registered September 3, 2014; nominated by Kristin Scholetzky

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the Woodstock Chamber of Commerce funded the tower. The Forest Service and the county library say the chamber supplied materials, and a 1947 note says citizens and the Forest Service built it cooperatively. The story reports both wordings; the 1935 build year and the CCC role agree wherever the sources give them.

notes_for_editor: No staffing history, fire-watch dates, or height figure was found in the sources read, so facts.height_m and staffing are omitted. The register's purpose (fire spotting plus recreation) and the county library's (tourism) differ in emphasis. A travel blog (thecommontraveler.net) says it was built to help rangers spot fires; it was not read and is not cited. The brief's elevation 557.8 m matches the register's 558 m. The brief's kind 'tower' matches 'Obs Tower' on firelookout.org. The Facebook and YouTube posts that surfaced in search were skipped as sources.
